stepNotes.1: Config spans source orchestration, schemas, JSONC paths, markdown expansion, TUI settings, and an isolated environment trust gate.
stepNotes.2: Source provenance controls whether project or remote input may execute, load code, resolve secret references, select providers, or grant permissions.
stepNotes.3: All explicitly untrusted inputs receive restricted substitution and field stripping, while updates preserve raw JSONC references under serialized mutation.
stepNotes.4: Directory I/O is parallel with ordered merge, dependency installs are serialized, and Instance/lazy caches keep work off steady-state paths.
stepNotes.5: Schemas and narrow path/markdown/trust helpers are well separated from the large config-impl orchestration hub.
stepNotes.6: The deprecated super_long migration module appears unimported and has a 2026-12-15 removal marker; the URL-parse empty catch is deliberate validation flow.
stepNotes.7: Tests strongly cover untrusted restrictions and update/install races; an exhaustive provenance-precedence matrix and removal-date assertion remain gaps.
stepNotes.8: CONFIG-001 remains verified-fixed, the recorded empty catch remains Low/deferred, and no new invariant violation was accepted.
stepNotes.9: The combined auth/config run passed 186 tests and core typechecking passed.
